proof.text: Fix a small quasicategory $Q$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ is the coherent nerve of the locally Kan simplicial category of small quasicategories with mapping Kan complexes $\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)^\simeq$, and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] gives natural equivalences $\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(X,Y)$ sending a functor to its edge and preserving composition with its coherent homotopies. Hence the homotopy category of $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ has as morphisms the classes of functors up to natural equivalence, with composition of functors, and each component $A\to A\prime$, $B\to B\prime$, $C\to C\prime$ of the objectwise equivalence, being an equivalence edge, is a functor equivalence: it has a quasi-inverse and coherent natural equivalences of both composites with the identities. By the cartesian-closure statement, postcomposition with each component is a map of coherent functor quasicategories $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,-)$, and passage to cores gives a map of the corresponding spaces. The quasi-inverse functors and the coherent inverse transformations give inverses after postcomposition; a natural equivalence restricts to a homotopy of cores because its components are equivalences ([lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences]). So each of the three vertex maps $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A\prime)^\simeq$, and likewise for $B$ and $C$, is an equivalence of spaces. The 2-simplices of the edge of cospan diagrams give, under the same identification, specified homotopies making the two squares of these postcomposition maps commute. The cone and core conventions are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, lines 77–80: functor-core diagrams and their componentwise equivalences; the coherent postcomposition expansion is written here.

proof.text: Apply the limiting-cone mapping-space criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] to the first cone, with ambient quasicategory $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ and test object $Q$. It makes $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,L)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,A)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,C)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,B)$ an equivalence, using the specified cone coherence. The natural composition-compatible equivalences $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,X)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,X)$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] (for $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ as in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration]) carry postcomposition of functors to postcomposition with the corresponding edges; by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-commuting-pullback-invariance] they induce an equivalence of the path pullbacks. Thus $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L)^\simeq$ is identified with the homotopy pullback of $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A)^\simeq$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)^\simeq$ over $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,C)^\simeq$. Applying the same to the second limiting cone gives the analogous comparison for $L\prime$ and the primed cospan.

proof.text: The compatible map of cones makes the two comparisons of Step 2 commute up to specified homotopy, by the naturality of the comparisons in maps of cones in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion]; this map is the one induced by the supplied cone map, including its square coherence. The right-hand map between the two path pullbacks is an equivalence: its three vertex maps are equivalences and its two squares commute by the specified homotopies of Step 1, so [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-commuting-pullback-invariance] applies.

proof.text: In the resulting square, commutative up to homotopy by Step 3, the two comparison maps from $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L)^\simeq$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L\prime)^\simeq$ to the path pullbacks are equivalences by Step 2 and the map between the path pullbacks is an equivalence by Step 3. The two-out-of-three property for equivalences of spaces therefore makes the top map $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L\prime)^\simeq$ an equivalence. This holds for every small quasicategory $Q$.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.5.3 proof, lines 81–94: equivalence of the test-core maps after comparing the two homotopy pullbacks.

proof.text: Since the test-core criterion [lem-coef-infinity-test-equivalence-by-functor-cores] applies to every small $Q$, the apex map $L\to L\prime$ is a functor equivalence, hence an equivalence edge of $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, since by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] the homotopy category of $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ composes classes of functors up to natural equivalence. Conversely, a functor equivalence has a coherent quasi-inverse; postcomposing with it and with the original map gives inverse maps on every coherent functor quasicategory and hence on their cores, by the coherent functor and cartesian-closure constructions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. Thus the functor-equivalence assertion and the displayed all-$Q$ mapping-space assertion are equivalent.

title: Equivalences of cospan diagrams induce equivalences of limiting apices
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, coherent cones, cores and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of small quasicategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and the limiting-cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion]. Consider two cospans $A\to C\leftarrow B$ and $A\prime\to C\prime\leftarrow B\prime$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, together with an objectwise equivalence between the cospans and a compatible map between coherent cones with apices $L$ and $L\prime$. If both cones are limiting, then the apex map $L\to L\prime$ is an equivalence in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Equivalently, for every small quasicategory $Q$, postcomposition induces an equivalence of spaces $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,L\prime)^\simeq$.
